candidate.answerReason: An odd sum of two primes forces one prime to be 2. The other is 83, giving product 166.

methods.label: Use the odd sum
methods.explanation:
Two odd numbers have an even sum. Since \(85\) is odd, one of the two primes must be even. The only even prime is \(2\), because every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself.

The other prime must therefore be \(85-2=83\), so their product is
\[
2\times83=166.
\]
The answer is \(166\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary odd-even reasoning and the definition of a prime number.

candidate.annotationRationale: The decisive target is recognizing the special role of 2 among primes. Parity determines that an even prime is needed, and the factor concept explains why no larger even prime exists.

review.mathematicalCheck: An odd sum forces an even prime, necessarily 2. The other number is 83, which is prime, and 2×83=166. The stated existence of two primes makes a separate primality test unnecessary in the solution.
review.levelCheck: The parity argument and explanation of the only even prime are elementary and complete.
